requirements.title: Machine-readable conformance evidence gates
Executable token transitions for an explicitly admitted BPMN subset
requirements.notes: The executable subset includes Standard Loops, FixedMultiInstance/1 and CollectionMultiInstance/1 on generic Tasks, and CatchEventChoice/1 for bounded Message/Timer Intermediate Catch Events. Both Multi-Instance profiles freeze one bounded closed member set at activation, preserve stable index identity, run sequentially or in parallel with behavior All, and either join all members or, when an admitted completionCondition first becomes true, terminate the already generated active remainder and mark a sequential planned suffix not-generated. CatchEventChoice/1 opens exact arms and atomically commits one deterministic winner, continuation, loser cancellation, and Message delivery disposition. Fingerprinted limits bound Timer lexical bytes, execution-state bytes, and transition-journal count/bytes beneath fixed parser/kernel ceilings; longer histories require a separate segmented/checkpoint protocol. SubProcess and CallActivity multi-instance execution, progressive behavior events, partial collection output, open or draining groups, and the broader BPMN Event lifecycle remain outside this kernel subset.

requirements.title: FixedMultiInstance/1 bounded generic Task execution
requirements.notes: This atomic executable profile is restricted to one generic Task with a version-bound formal loopCardinality, behavior absent or All, sequential or parallel execution, an optional version-bound formal completionCondition, and a compiled maximum cardinality. Cardinality is evaluated once before member creation. Durable group/member state records stable index and item identity, exact active/completed/terminated counters over generated instances, first-true completion cancellation, a distinct not-generated sequential suffix, Boundary Error or failure cleanup, late-completion fencing, and causal journal replay. XML v6 can represent broader collection and One/None/Complex metadata, but this cardinality profile does not silently adopt it; collection scatter/gather is covered only by the separate CollectionMultiInstance/1 requirement. It does not claim SubProcess or CallActivity multi-instance execution, progressive behavior events, open WCP15 groups, draining WCP34/WCP36 joins, or a complete BPMN Activity lifecycle.

requirements.title: CollectionMultiInstance/1 bounded collection-driven generic Task execution
requirements.notes: This atomic executable profile is restricted to one generic Task whose exact externally compiled binding for loopDataInputRef evaluates once at activation to a bounded canonical JSON array. Membership, source indices, order, and duplicate values are frozen before expansion; empty input creates no work. A scalar inputDataItem explicitly opts into current-item mapping, and absence forbids implicit injection. Complete output gathering requires loopDataOutputRef, a scalar outputDataItem, a matching collection-valued Task DataOutput, and a protocol-v3 Task binding; every member output is codec-validated and gathered by source index, with empty input yielding an empty output array. Output gathering with completionCondition is rejected until a partial-result policy is selected. Data documents, expression and collection bindings, Task bindings, and byte/cardinality limits are fingerprinted external compile inputs rather than semantics inferred from BPMN XML alone. Parallel all-join execution supplies the bounded WCP14 runtime-known case. This does not claim progressive behavior, externalized or streaming item manifests, SubProcess or CallActivity multi-instance execution, open WCP15 creation, WCP34/WCP36, a mandatory Effect Workflow backend, or complete BPMN Process Execution Conformance.

requirements.title: Protocol-bound Task outcomes and interrupting Boundary Error execution slice
requirements.notes: This atomic slice admits an immutable protocol-v3 binding on a generic Task, one-execution translation from a native managed-retry result, exact application-failure-to-BPMN-Error promotion, and at most one interrupting Boundary Error. The XML executable facade accepts task bindings explicitly through CompileXmlOptions and commits them to the executable fingerprint; bindings remain external executable inputs and are not inferred from BPMN XML. Schedule-to-close timeout remains operational and is not treated as a BPMN Error or Boundary Timer. This is not evidence for the complete Activity lifecycle, generic event propagation, BPMN Cancel, Boundary Timer or Timer semantics outside CatchEventChoice/1, non-interrupting boundaries, or event subprocesses.

requirements.title: CatchEventChoice/1 Message and Timer Intermediate Catch Event execution slice
requirements.notes: CatchEventChoice/1 admits only normal-flow Intermediate Catch Events with one Message definition or one Timer definition containing exactly one timeDuration or timeDate. Waiting opens when the event is reached and one accepted occurrence is consumed before continuation. Message admission uses an externally compiled exact ordered non-empty key-correlation expression, payload contract, and authorization-policy build. The atomic delivery transition is the acceptedAt authority: every previously unseen receipt.acceptedAt must equal services.now while the exact active arm, correlation, policy pin, payload bound, and race winner or fence are validated; a sender timestamp is never authoritative, while exact redelivery of an already committed receipt remains idempotent. timeDuration and timeDate remain BPMN tExpression values. The profile requires their evaluated value to be a string and parses that string as a bounded ISO-8601/XML Schema duration or dateTime subset; this runtime restriction is not a direct XSD constraint on the tExpression text. The profile is transient-active-only and has no early-message inbox. A global deliveryId ledger consumes both Message winners and Messages preempted by a Timer. Timer deadlines and correlation results are recorded for causal replay without clock or expression reexecution. Signal, Conditional, Multiple, Parallel Multiple, timeCycle, Start, Boundary, throwing, Receive Task, and event-subprocess semantics are excluded. BPMN Table 10.99 requires operationRef for Message Events in executable Processes, while this slice rejects operationRef and uses the external fingerprinted MessageBinding. BPMN 13.3.3 also describes predicate correlation, which this exact-key profile rejects. Therefore this is implementation-profile evidence, not complete BPMN Process Execution Conformance.

requirements.title: CatchEventChoice/1 exclusive non-instantiating Event-Based Gateway execution slice
requirements.notes: CatchEventChoice/1 admits one diverging exclusive non-instantiating Event-Based Gateway with one incoming flow and between two and the compiled maximum number of unique unconditional direct Message/Timer catch branches. It atomically opens every arm. The atomic delivery transition requires every previously unseen receipt.acceptedAt to equal services.now and compares that authoritative instant with every materialized Timer deadline; a Timer wins equality and equal Timer deadlines use immutable branch ordinal. One transition commits the winner, continuation, and cancellation of all losing arms and Timers. Current-time late or stale Message deliveries are fenced, backdated deliveries are rejected, and exact duplicate or Timer-preempted deliveries are replayed through causal facts. Instantiating and Parallel Event-Based Gateways remain excluded by this execution profile; at the BPMN model foundation, a Parallel Event-Based Gateway is valid only when instantiate is true. Receive Task branches, additional incoming flows, conditional/default branches, and non-Message/Timer event configurations also remain excluded. This bounded first-trigger/withdraw-losers slice is not the complete BPMN Event-Based Gateway surface or Process Execution Conformance.

requirements.title: Executable intersection of the named core-process XML profile and token kernel
requirements.notes: This is a deliberately narrower executable admission profile, not Process Execution Conformance. Profile bpmn-2.0.2-core-process-di-v6 admits while-style pre-test and BPMN post-tested Standard Loops plus FixedMultiInstance/1 and CollectionMultiInstance/1 only on generic Tasks, and CatchEventChoice/1 for standalone Message/Timer catches or an exclusive non-instantiating Message/Timer Event-Based Gateway. FixedMultiInstance/1 requires a version-bound loopCardinality. CollectionMultiInstance/1 requires exact external data and collection bindings, freezes one bounded array at activation, preserves indices/order/duplicates, exposes items only through scalar inputDataItem, and optionally gathers a complete codec-validated output array through loopDataOutputRef plus scalar outputDataItem. CatchEventChoice/1 requires exact external Message bindings and excludes operationRef, timeCycle, other event definitions, retained early Messages, Start/Boundary/Receive/event-subprocess catches, and instantiating/Parallel event gateways. Unsupported process, gateway, event, activity, combined-loop, SubProcess-loop, progressive behavior, partial output, open-group, and implicit-activation semantics are rejected rather than inferred.

source.section: tDefinitions, tProcess, tActivity, tStandardLoopCharacteristics, tMultiInstanceLoopCharacteristics, tIntermediateCatchEvent, tMessageEventDefinition, tTimerEventDefinition, tEventBasedGateway, flow nodes, and tSequenceFlow

requirements.notes: Profile bpmn-2.0.2-core-process-di-v6 covers ordinary processes and recursive subprocesses, generic tasks, source-level callActivity callable-element QNames, none start/end events, exclusive/parallel gateways, sequence flows, conditions, defaults, definitions metadata, explicit expression-version bindings, Standard Loop characteristics, the represented tMultiInstanceLoopCharacteristics fields on generic Tasks, normal-flow Message/Timer Intermediate Catch Events, and exclusive non-instantiating Event-Based Gateways. Catch XML round-trips one local Message definition without operationRef or one Timer timeDuration/timeDate definition, plus direct unconditional gateway branches; timeCycle, other Event definitions, multiple/parallel-multiple catches, Receive Tasks, and instantiating/Parallel event gateways fail closed. timeDuration and timeDate are tExpression content, so the XML layer does not claim that XSD directly constrains their text to xsd:duration or xsd:dateTime. Executable admission instead evaluates the expression, requires a string, and parses a bounded ISO-8601/XML Schema duration or dateTime subset. Multi-instance XML can round-trip cardinality, collection references, scalar inputDataItem/outputDataItem declarations with namespace-expanded itemSubjectRef QNames and xsd:string names including the empty string, sequential/parallel mode, completionCondition, behavior, and One/None event references in BPMN XSD order. Executable collection, Message, authorization, and correlation semantics additionally require fingerprinted external bindings. Call activities are interchange-only until immutable child-target resolution and durable parent/child execution exist. This is a fail-closed implementation slice, not an OMG conformance subclass, complete semantic mapping, or general event/multi-instance profile.

requirements.title: Normative Activity lifecycle and operational semantics
Interrupting boundary Event operational semantics
requirements.notes: A modeled boundary Event with cancelActivity=true cancels its attached Activity and follows the boundary Sequence Flow; a Multi-Instance attachment cancels all instances. This requirement is distinct from an external control-plane withdrawal.

requirements.title: Terminate End Event operational semantics
requirements.notes: Terminate is reached by modeled control flow, ends the current Process scope without compensation or event handling, and at Sub-Process level does not terminate higher or sibling instances. OperationalInstanceWithdrawal/1 is not evidence for this requirement.

requirements.title: Transaction Sub-Process Cancel Event semantics
requirements.notes: CancelEventDefinition is restricted to Transaction Sub-Processes. Transaction cancellation can include rollback and compensation before control leaves through the Cancel boundary. No external operational withdrawal may claim this meaning.

requirements.title: Compensation handler and triggering semantics
requirements.notes: Compensation reverses effects of successfully completed Activities through explicit handlers; an active Activity must be canceled instead. Logical withdrawal without handler execution is not compensation evidence.

requirements.title: Control-flow pattern catalogue
requirements.notes: Family requirement only. Atomic control-flow requirements are being admitted separately; prose coverage is not implementation evidence.

requirements.title: WCP1 Sequence
WCP2 Parallel Split
WCP3 Synchronization
WCP4 Exclusive Choice
WCP16 Deferred Choice - transient Message/Timer subset
requirements.notes: CatchEventChoice/1 supplies the bounded transient-trigger form of Deferred Choice: all exact Message/Timer alternatives remain enabled after the gateway opens, one accepted trigger wins, and winner routing plus withdrawal of all losers is atomic. The delivery transition requires receipt.acceptedAt to equal services.now; that atomic acceptance instant and materialized Timer deadlines define the deterministic race. A Timer wins equality and equal Timers use immutable branch order. Late and duplicate deliveries are fenced, and replay consumes the recorded winner without rerunning the race. Early-message retention, persistent triggers, human work, Receive Tasks, signals, conditions, multiple events, and broader Event-Based Gateway configurations require different profiles and are not WCP16 evidence here.

requirements.title: WCP19 Cancel Task
requirements.notes: WCP19 withdraws one enabled or running task, removes work-list references, and emits no normal continuation. OperationalInstanceWithdrawal/1 has no targeted task or work-item command and therefore does not claim WCP19.

requirements.title: WCP20 Cancel Case
requirements.notes: WCP20 withdraws a complete process instance, including current and future tasks and all subprocesses, from an internal or external trigger, and records unsuccessful completion. OperationalInstanceWithdrawal/1 supplies only bounded logical case withdrawal and excludes executable CallActivity descendants, work items, human tasks, and physical-stop guarantees.

requirements.title: OperationalInstanceWithdrawal/1 external control-plane extension
requirements.notes: The successful portable commit/CAS of the request and scheduling fence is the linearization point. requestId is idempotent; rootScopeInstanceId, WithdrawalAuditAttribution, and optional reasonCode are audited; owned embedded scopes, loop/gateway frames, fixed/collection Multi-Instance groups, catch waits, subscriptions, and timers close without outgoing flow; late task outcomes are fenced. The profile is never BPMN Cancel, Terminate, compensation, rollback, or proof that an external side effect stopped.

requirements.title: WCP13 Multiple Instances with a Priori Design-Time Knowledge - fixed Task subset
requirements.notes: FixedMultiInstance/1 covers WCP13 only when the pinned cardinality expression represents a fixed design-time model value: parallel mode creates the closed set of independent, stably identified members and produces one continuation only after every member has completed. Sequential mode is supported by the BPMN profile but is not used as evidence for the pattern's concurrent form. The same runtime primitive instead admits WCP14 when the expression obtains its value from activation data.

requirements.title: WCP14 Multiple Instances with a Priori Run-Time Knowledge - frozen Task subset
requirements.notes: FixedMultiInstance/1 evaluates one runtime cardinality before creating any member. CollectionMultiInstance/1 instead snapshots one bounded collection with stable source indices, order, and duplicates before expansion. Both freeze a closed member set and join all members before one continuation; parallel mode is the WCP14 evidence and sequential mode is an additional BPMN execution form. Neither admits new members after activation, so WCP15 is not claimed.

requirements.title: WCP35 Cancelling Partial Join for Multiple Instances - completionCondition subset
requirements.notes: The admitted WCP35 evidence is the parallel closed-group subset. A pinned BPMN completionCondition is evaluated after every committed logical member completion. The first true result produces one continuation and terminates every already generated active remainder; a sequential planned suffix is never generated or counted as terminated. FixedMultiInstance/1 and CollectionMultiInstance/1 both admit this behavior, but the collection profile rejects output gathering in the same group until an explicit partial-result policy exists. This does not claim WCP15 open creation, WCP34 remainder draining, or WCP36 dynamic creation/draining. Those require a separate OpenForEachGroup/1 profile.

requirements.title: WCP21 Structured Loop - bounded generic Task subset
requirements.notes: This atomic requirement is scoped to executable while-style pre-test and BPMN post-tested behavior for one generic Task, with durable iteration identity, exact condition evidence whose true result means continue, and a mandatory positive iteration cap. It does not claim WCP21's combined pre/post-test variant, Standard Loops on SubProcesses, arbitrary cycles, or any multi-instance pattern. BPMN 2.0.2 section 13.3.6 explicitly maps Structured Loop to WCP-21; section 10.3.8 and Table 10.28 define the Standard Loop condition, testBefore default, and loopMaximum cap.
